title: Talanx posts record nine months as losses run €750M below budget
full_text:
Talanx, the name behind HDI and Hannover Re, posted a record nine-month group net income of €2.195 billion in its third-quarter results, up 12% on the same period a year earlier. Chief executive officer Torsten Leue pointed directly to the mechanism: large loss payments came in roughly €750 million below the pro rata budget for the period, and the net investment result jumped 52% to €1.5 billion, partly from the structural shift to higher-yield assets in prior years and partly from realised gains on asset sales.
The combined ratio improved to 89.0% from 89.8%. The corporate and specialty division, home of HDI Global, improved its nine-month combined ratio to 90.3% from 91.6% on stable revenue of €7.6 billion, with large losses running below both the prior year and budget. The division’s net income contribution rose 11% to €455 million.
The three largest individual loss events named in the release were the Colombia earthquake (€270 million), Atlantic storms on the Iberian peninsula and in Morocco (€137 million), and Winter Storm Fern in the US and Canada (€109 million). None of those events have direct Australian or New Zealand exposure in the nine-month figures. No Australian cat event features individually in the release, in contrast to years when Queensland flooding or NSW storms have contributed materially to Hannover Re’s results. Leue said if large losses remain substantially below expectation through year-end, Talanx intends to further strengthen its balance sheet.
That balance sheet trajectory matters for Australian and New Zealand brokers placing property catastrophe and specialty risks through Hannover Re, whose appetite and terms at treaty renewals are shaped in part by the parent group’s capital position.
For brokers placing corporate and specialty risks through HDI Global in Australia and New Zealand, the group result provides the financial backdrop for the branch’s own expansion. HDI Global Australia surpassed 230 international programmes written out of the branch in the first half of 2026 and opened a representative office in Seoul, targeting international programmes, captive solutions, and renewable energy across the Asia-Pacific region. The Seoul office added K-pop event cancellation cover and surety bonds for Korean contractors to the branch’s specialty offering, while core underwriting remains in Hong Kong.
As HDI Global’s Australian operations have expanded under Stefan Feldmann’s Asia-Pacific leadership, the branch has also added environmental impairment liability and film and production liability to its specialty lines. A parent group posting a 90.3% corporate and specialty combined ratio, with losses running €750 million below budget and a Solvency II ratio of 241%, is not funding that expansion from a constrained capital position.
Talanx lifted its full-year 2026 net income forecast to more than €2.8 billion and set a 2027 target of more than €3 billion for the first time. The €200 million Iran war reserve booked in Q2 remains an open variable in the nine-month figures.
